title: Affine formal equivalence with quotient-system and section-limit natural comparisons
statement: Let X be an affine Noetherian scheme, J ideal sheaf data, and Coh(X,J) the coherent formal category [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. Put A=Gamma(X,top), I=J(top), S=AdicCompletion I A [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Let F be the full category of finite S-modules, R:F to Mod_A scalar restriction, L=tilde followed by pullback along X.isoSpec [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections], and C=L followed by formalCompletionFunctor J. Let W send a formal system to its actual diagram of top section A-modules. There exist an equivalence E:F equivalent to Coh(X,J), a natural isomorphism beta:E.functor followed by the formal-system inclusion isomorphic to R followed by C, and a natural isomorphism gamma:R isomorphic to E.functor followed by the inclusion, W and categorical lim. Both comparisons apply to every finite S-module and every S-linear map. No presentation, chosen formal map, eta, torsion condition or annihilator estimate is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 087W, lemma-inverse-systems-affine, together with the canonical affine chart (01IB) and completion comparisons (00MA, 05GG)

proof.text: Use the canonical affine chart and transport top sections and the top ideal. The top-ideal identity is verified by ext_of_isAffine and isoSpec.inv.appTop=GammaSpecIso.inv. Apply the natural affine Spec transport on the top open, identifying its open subscheme with X via the top immersion. Compose the resulting equivalence with the inverse of the Spec finite-completed-module equivalence. This gives E from finite S-modules to coherent formal systems.

The Spec inverse comparison is the sheaf quotient system of the restricted finite completed module. On each level n+1, the affine quotient comparison identifies the sheaf quotient C(Q)_n with the chart pullback of tilde(Q/I^(n+1)Q), including its projection. Finite S-modules are complete, as incorporated in the Spec equivalence. The quotient comparisons transport its inverse realization to X. Naturality for transition maps and module maps follows by precomposing with the quotient projection, which is epimorphic, and cancelling it. These levelwise comparisons form beta:E.functor followed by the formal inclusion isomorphic to R followed by C.

The Spec equivalence supplies natural limiting cones on the section systems, with vertex the restricted S-module. Transport these cones using the Spec-transport section isomorphism. Restriction along topIso.inv and the top-open identification cancels, giving A-module cones on the actual top sections on X. The limit universal property identifies each cone vertex with the categorical limit, giving gamma:R isomorphic to E.functor followed by the formal inclusion, top section diagrams and lim. To verify naturality compose with every projection; the equations follow from naturality of the supplied cones and transported section isomorphisms, and jointly monomorphic projections give equality. The same calculations work for I=0, I=A, the empty scheme and zero modules.

lean.statement:
theorem coherentFormalModules_affine_global_comparison
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsNoetherian X] [IsAffine X] (J : X.IdealSheafData) :
    let A := Γ(X, ⊤)
    let I := J.ideal ⟨⊤, isAffineOpen_top X⟩
    let S := AdicCompletion I A
    let F := ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory
      (fun Q : ModuleCat.{u} S ↦ Module.Finite S Q)
    let R := ObjectProperty.ι (fun Q : ModuleCat.{u} S ↦ Module.Finite S Q) ⋙
      ModuleCat.restrictScalars (algebraMap A S)
    let C := tilde.functor A ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback X.isoSpec.hom ⋙
      formalCompletionFunctor J
    let W := (Functor.whiskeringRight ℕᵒᵖ X.Modules (ModuleCat A)).obj
      (SheafOfModules.evaluation X.ringCatSheaf (op ⊤))
    ∃ E : F ≌ CoherentFormalModule X J,
      Nonempty (E.functor ⋙ (IsCoherentFormalModule J).ι ≅ R ⋙ C) ∧
      Nonempty (R ≅ E.functor ⋙ (IsCoherentFormalModule J).ι ⋙ W ⋙ lim)
